# Pi Contract Upgrade Trail — llms.txt
# A read-only, zero-dependency timeline builder for Soroban contract deployments
# on Pi Network; flags every wasmHash change as an upgrade.

> Soroban contracts CAN be upgraded by replacing the stored wasmHash. This tool
> turns a deployments manifest into a per-contract history and surfaces hash
> changes at a glance.

## What it is
- read-only, zero-dependency, Node (ESM), Node >= 18
- upgrade-trail.mjs: the CLI (--manifest --network --offline)
- test.mjs: 14 offline checks (node --test)
- never writes; no database; no API keys

## Why it exists
Anyone auditing a Pi contract needs to answer: has this contract ever been
changed, and when? A manifest of deployments makes that answerable; this tool
makes the answer readable.

## Input format
Any nested JSON containing objects with contractId (or contract_id) and
optionally wasmHash, deployTx, timestamp, name. The loader walks the whole tree,
so flat or nested manifests both work. Snake_case keys are accepted.

## Output shape
Per contract: [n] hash=<wasmHash> tx=<deployTx> ts=<timestamp> <first_seen|UPGRADE>.
Then per contract: recorded deployments, upgrades (hash changes).

## Measured constraints (2026-10-19, protocol 28)
- No measured RPC method returns a contract's CURRENT wasmHash.
  getContractData is not implemented ("method not found"); getLedgerEntries
  exists but needs a base64 ledger key this tool does not build.
- There is no public Soroban RPC on Mainnet: rpc.mainnet.minepi.com answers
  HTTP 503 and serves a certificate that expired 2023-05-30.

## Usage
- node upgrade-trail.mjs --manifest deployments/testnet.json
- node upgrade-trail.mjs --manifest deployments/testnet.json --network mainnet
- node upgrade-trail.mjs --manifest deployments/testnet.json --offline
- node --test test.mjs
Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 invalid JSON or missing file.
--offline exists so the timeline logic is verifiable deterministically without
depending on RPC availability.

## Not claimed
- that a single entry proves no earlier deployment (the manifest records only
  what the deploy script logged; absence of an entry is not evidence of absence)
- that the on-chain contract still matches the last wasmHash (no measured RPC
  method returns it)
- that the deployer is a known or trusted party (on-chain data never proves
  venue or team ownership)
- that Mainnet was checked live (there is no public Soroban RPC on Mainnet)
- that Pi Network has adopted, reviewed or endorsed this
